reason: The text explicitly presents the land of Canaan as a crucial element of what matters to Yahweh. God repeatedly emphasizes his covenant to give the land to the descendants of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob (e.g., 'וְגַ֨ם הֲקִמֹ֤תִי אֶת־ בְּרִיתִי֙ אִתָּ֔ם לָתֵ֥ת לָהֶ֖ם אֶת־ אֶ֣רֶץ כְּנָ֑עַן'—'I established my covenant with them to give them the land of Canaan'). The promise of the land is presented as foundational to God's covenant, appearing multiple times throughout the passage as the ultimate fulfillment of God's oath to the patriarchs. The land is not merely incidental but integral to what God seeks to accomplish for his people.
